# Wagner Logistics to Add Nearly 80 Jobs with New High-Volume Logistics Operation in Liberty

 Wagner Logistics 

Oct 14, 2026, 08:54 ET

NORTH KANSAS CITY, Mo., Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Wagner Logistics, a nationwide provider of third-party logistics, today announced it has signed a multi-year agreement with a Kansas City-area manufacturer to launch a new manufacturing support and warehouse operations program in Liberty, Mo.

The new operation includes two leased warehouse facilities in the Liberty area totaling more than 830,000 square feet. Wagner expects to add 79 new local jobs over the next two years, starting immediately. The company will also make a multi-million-dollar investment in equipment, infrastructure and automated trailer loading and unloading technology to support the operation.

"This is exactly the kind of operation where Wagner's strengths come through," said Brian Smith, President and Chief Executive Officer of Wagner Logistics. "It requires speed, flexibility, close coordination and the ability to design a solution around what the customer actually needs."

Averitt Adds 100,000-Sq.-Ft. Mississippi Warehouse

# Averitt adds 100,000-sq.ft. Warehouse to Mississippi Freight Campus

Written by WarehouseArc Newsroom • August 28, 2026

Averitt has opened a 100,000-square-foot warehouse beside its existing 57-door LTL terminal in Richland, Mississippi, putting distribution, fulfillment and asset-based freight operations on the same logistics campus.

The Jackson Distribution & Fulfillment facility opened August 24 at 109 Diane Drive, near the intersection of Interstates 20 and 55.

Rather than operating solely as a dedicated warehouse for a single customer, the building is configured as a multi-tenant facility where Averitt is offering space without long-term warehouse contracts.

That gives the 3PL capacity for customers seeking temporary inventory space as well as more conventional distribution and fulfillment operations. Averitt is marketing the building for requirements including overflow inventory, seasonal storage and emergency staging, with customers able to adjust the amount of space they use as requirements change.

The operational proposition extends beyond the additional square footage.
